question.problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An elementary matrix is a matrix obtained from the identity matrix by applying exactly one elementary row operation. 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- The matrix $A$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:=(-2){R}_{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{2}:=(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =A\end{aligned}
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not an elementary matrix because it can't be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying only one elementary row operation.

- The matrix $C$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are elementary matrices.
